size.note: Sierra black bears 1.2-1.9 m head and body (measured along the spine), 0.7-0.9 m at the shoulder; tail a stub of 8-14 cm. The build turns the generated head back to the midline, lengthens the bear 1.12x and scales it to 0.8 m at the withers: 1.34 m nose to rump in a straight line. Cubs are drawn at 0.45x (animals.js), sows 0.92x, boars 1.06x.

source.prompt: An American black bear (Ursus americanus) of the Sierra Nevada, California, NOT a grizzly: no shoulder hump, a straight face profile and tall rounded ears. One adult standing still on all four legs, side-on neutral pose, legs straight with clear gaps between them, big flat paws with short dark claws, head level and a little lower than the shoulders. Realistic proportions: 80 cm at the shoulder, 1.5 m head and body, a heavy round body, the rump as high as the shoulders, short thick legs, a tiny stub tail. Dark brown fur, tan muzzle, black nose, small dark eyes. No base, no ground. Game-ready.

rig: skinned, the standard quadruped skeleton of 20 joints (tools/rig_quadruped.py, 2026-10-30): Hips, Spine, Chest, Neck, Head, Tail1-3 and per leg UpperLeg (shoulder or hip), LowerLeg (elbow or stifle) and Foot (wrist or hock to the toe), FL FR HL HR; posture plantigrade, the wrist at 0.4 and the hock at 0.45 of the elbow's and stifle's height, the joints centred on the leg columns, a vertex ring cut at each joint; weights by height along each leg with short blends, the arm and thigh skin fading into the upper bone, the trunk Hips / Spine / Chest by z, the head part Neck / Head, the tail by its arc. Posed live by the leg engine (client/src/gait.js: planted feet, two-bone IK, the gaits by the Froude bands of the locomotion row) near the eye, by its baked cycles beyond. The part attributes stay for the fallback. Before: quadruped template Q: BODY, LEG_A (left fore + right hind), LEG_B, TAIL (the stub, pivot at its root), HEAD (neck and head, pivot at the neck's base; kept off the chest and the tops of the forelegs). No TAIL_TIP. Parts found from the geometry (the stub within ~8 cm of the rump's farthest point, legs below the belly line between the feet with pivots there: elbow and stifle, head ahead of a vertical plane at the neck's base); weights blended over 5-12 cm. Pivots and the bedded drop (0.19 m) in extras.rig. lod2 is decimated in two passes (the body with the head kept, then the head) so the far tier keeps a snout and ears.
accuracy_notes: Generated, not adopted from a download: no CC0 or CC BY black bear mesh reads as one. Reads as a black bear, not a grizzly: no shoulder hump (the top line is nearly level: the fur over the shoulders stands about 3 cm above the hips, a long gentle rise, not a muscled hump), a straight face profile with a long snout, tall rounded ears up on the crown, short curved claws, a heavy round body on short thick legs, a stub tail. Coloured as a brown-phase Sierra bear: dark brown body, darker back and legs, a little lighter belly, tan snout to the eyes, black nose pad. Fixed by the build: the head was turned 17-19 degrees to the bear's left (turned back about a vertical axis behind the ears); the body was short (lengthened 1.12x). Still wrong or unchecked: the eye is one dark face behind the stop at every tier (the head is a smooth low-poly sculpt with no modelled eye); the generator's fur shards make the lod0 flanks faceted; the far tier is boxy; no cinnamon or black phase yet (a second colour set would do it); one bear size for both sexes (instances scaled). Check the snout length, the ear size and the brown against Yosemite photos.
